Chapter 10: The Meaning of Care — Reflections on Life, Death, and What Remains.
As the years went by, Sandra found herself looking deeper into the meaning behind her work. You know, trauma cleaning wasn’t just about tidying up after tragedy—it became, for her, almost like a meditation on life, death, and what’s left behind when it’s all over.
Every job reminded her how temporary everything is. Imagine seeing a whole life reduced to just a few boxes, a collection of memories, and a handful of belongings. It hits you—how quickly things can fade.
But even among the mess, Sandra would stumble across little moments of beauty. Maybe it was a faded photograph someone once treasured, set gently on a mantel. Or a child’s drawing, hidden away in a drawer for years. Sometimes, she’d find a letter never sent, words of love and regret waiting quietly on the page. These small treasures—they were a gentle reminder that every single life matters. Every story, no matter how quiet, is worth honoring.
Over time, Sandra realized that real care wasn’t just about cleaning up after someone had gone. It was about affirming life—treating everyone with dignity, no matter their situation. It was her way of saying, “You mattered. You were seen. You were loved.”
This work also made Sandra think about her own life, and what she’d leave behind. She wondered: what will people remember? Not the clutter or the mess, but those moments of kindness—the times she helped someone find hope again.
Sandra’s journey isn’t only about cleaning up after heartbreak. It’s about the courage to face life’s messes head on, to search for meaning even in the middle of chaos, and to offer hope when it’s needed most.
And maybe, that’s the biggest lesson of all: no matter how broken things look, there’s always a way to begin again.
